_readme: Every assumption behind the theatrical profit estimate. Edit, then rerun `python build_dashboard.py` (no re-ingest needed). Rates are fractions of box office gross; money is in US dollars.

rental_rates._readme: Studio share of gross ('rentals'). international_ex_china and china apply only to films whose data includes a China split (china_gross). Everything else gets international_blended on all international gross. worldwide_only applies when a film has a worldwide figure but no domestic/international split.

_pa_tiers_basis_readme: 'real' (default): budgets are converted to latest-CPI-year dollars before picking a tier, and flat P&A amounts are read as latest-year dollars, then deflated back to the film's release year. This stops a $10.5M 1982 film from being charged a modern $12M marketing spend. 'nominal': tiers apply to the reported budget as-is.
_pa_tiers_readme: A film takes the first tier whose bound contains its budget (budget < max_budget, or <= when max_inclusive). kind 'percent_of_budget' charges value x budget; kind 'flat' charges value dollars. The last tier must have max_budget null. These tiers also define the dashboard's budget-tier filter and grouping.
_roi_table_min_budget_readme: Films with a budget below this (in the dollars currently displayed) are left out of the top/bottom 25 ROI tables so micro-budget outliers do not swamp them.
